sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: AWS gives customers different ways to purchase compute and storage because different workloads have different requirements. The exam wants you to recognize which pricing option fits the workload.
bullets: Compute purchasing options: On-Demand Instances, Reserved Instances, Spot Instances, AWS Savings Plans, Dedicated Hosts, Dedicated Instances, and Capacity Reservations
Understanding Reserved Instance flexibility and Reserved Instances in AWS Organizations
Understanding incoming and outgoing data-transfer costs
Understanding pricing differences among storage options and tiers
sections.callout: Which pricing option fits the workload?

sections.title: Maestro Mental Model
bullets: KNOW I WILL USE IT → Reserved Instances
OLD OR RARE DATA → Lower-cost storage options
sections.callout: Match commitment, interruption tolerance, isolation, capacity, transfer direction, and access frequency to the pricing choice.

sections.title: On-Demand Instances
paragraphs: On-Demand Instances let customers use EC2 compute capacity without making a long-term commitment. They provide flexibility for short-term, unpredictable, irregular workloads that are not suitable for a long-term commitment.

entries.title: Scenario
paragraphs: A company is launching a new application and does not yet know how much compute it will need.

sections.callout: ON-DEMAND = USE IT WHEN I NEED IT

sections.title: Reserved Instances
paragraphs: Reserved Instances provide billing discounts compared with equivalent On-Demand usage when customers make a longer-term commitment. They make sense for predictable workloads where customers expect sustained usage.

entries.title: Scenario
paragraphs: A company knows an application will run continuously for a long period.
entries.recognitionCue: Predictable workload + long-term commitment + discount compared with On-Demand → Reserved Instances

sections.callout: RESERVED = COMMIT FOR SAVINGS

sections.title: Reserved Instance Flexibility
paragraphs: Not all Reserved Instances provide identical flexibility. AWS provides different RI options that can vary in the ability to change certain attributes. Do not assume every reservation behaves exactly the same way.
sections.callout: More flexibility may come with different discount tradeoffs.

sections.title: Reserved Instances and AWS Organizations
paragraphs: AWS Organizations can provide consolidated billing across accounts. Under applicable conditions, Reserved Instance pricing benefits can be shared across accounts in an organization. The exam may describe multiple AWS accounts under one organization and ask about sharing eligible pricing benefits.
sections.callout: ORGANIZATION = BILLING BENEFITS CAN CROSS ACCOUNTS

sections.title: Spot Instances
paragraphs: Spot Instances use spare EC2 capacity at significant discounts, but AWS can interrupt the capacity. Spot is appropriate for workloads that can tolerate interruptions, including batch processing, flexible workloads, fault-tolerant processing, and jobs that can restart.

entries.title: Scenario
paragraphs: A company has a large batch-processing job that can stop and resume later.

sections.callout: SPOT = CHEAP BUT INTERRUPTIBLE

sections.title: Exam Trap — On-Demand vs. Reserved vs. Spot

table.caption: Choose by the workload's defining requirement
rows: Interruption tolerance; spare capacity at a discount

sections.callout: ON-DEMAND = NOW · RESERVED = COMMIT · SPOT = CHEAP BUT INTERRUPTIBLE

sections.title: AWS Savings Plans
paragraphs: AWS Savings Plans offer savings in exchange for committing to a consistent amount of compute usage over a specified term. Depending on the plan, Savings Plans can provide more flexibility than tying the discount exclusively to one exact instance configuration.
sections.callout: SAVINGS PLAN = COMMIT TO COMPUTE SPEND OR USAGE

sections.title: Reserved Instances vs. Savings Plans

table.caption: Separate the two commitment models
rows: Discounted EC2 usage associated with reservation attributes
Commitment to consistent compute usage or spend with flexibility depending on the plan

sections.callout: RI = RESERVATION · SAVINGS PLAN = COMPUTE COMMITMENT

sections.title: Dedicated Hosts
paragraphs: A Dedicated Host is a physical server dedicated to a single AWS customer. It can be important for compliance requirements, licensing requirements, server-bound software licensing, and visibility or control over physical server placement.
sections.callout: Need an entire physical server dedicated to one customer → Dedicated Host

sections.title: Dedicated Instances
paragraphs: Dedicated Instances run on hardware dedicated to a single customer. They do not provide the same level of host-level visibility or control as Dedicated Hosts.
sections.callout: DEDICATED INSTANCE = ISOLATED HARDWARE

sections.title: Exam Trap — Dedicated Host vs. Dedicated Instance

table.caption: Separate physical-host control from tenant isolation
rows: Physical server visibility or control, or certain licensing requirements
Instances on single-customer hardware without the same host-level control

sections.callout: HOST = CONTROL THE HOUSE · INSTANCE = YOUR TENANT IS ISOLATED

sections.title: Capacity Reservations
paragraphs: An On-Demand Capacity Reservation reserves EC2 capacity in a particular Availability Zone. Its primary goal is capacity availability, not a pricing discount.

entries.title: Scenario
paragraphs: A company must ensure EC2 capacity will be available in a specific Availability Zone when needed.
entries.recognitionCue: Guarantee or reserve EC2 capacity → Capacity Reservation

sections.callout: CAPACITY RESERVATION = SAVE ME A SEAT

sections.title: Exam Trap — Reserved Instance vs. Capacity Reservation

table.caption: Do not let the word reservation decide the answer
rows: Capacity availability in a specific Availability Zone

sections.callout: RI = PRICING BENEFIT · CAPACITY RESERVATION = SAVE CAPACITY

sections.title: Data Transfer Pricing
paragraphs: AWS data-transfer pricing depends on where data is moving. Data entering AWS from the internet is often free, while data leaving AWS can cost money. Exact pricing varies by service and transfer path, and data movement between AWS Regions can also incur charges. Network architecture can therefore affect cost.
sections.callout: DATA IN IS OFTEN FREE · DATA OUT CAN COST MONEY

sections.title: Same Region vs. Different Regions
paragraphs: Pricing for moving data between resources can depend on the service, Availability Zone, Region, and direction of transfer. Never assume all AWS network transfers are free.
sections.callout: DATA LOCATION CAN AFFECT PRICE

sections.title: Storage Pricing
paragraphs: Storage cost depends on the storage service, amount of data, storage class or tier, access frequency, retrieval requirements, data transfer, and operations or requests. This connects directly to the storage services learned in Task Statement 3.6.
sections.callout: Choose the storage option by workload and access pattern.

sections.title: Storage Tiers
paragraphs: Frequently accessed data generally has different pricing characteristics from rarely accessed archival data. Frequent-access tiers are optimized for immediate use. Archive tiers are optimized for lower-cost long-term retention with different retrieval characteristics.
sections.callout: FREQUENT ACCESS = IMMEDIATE USE · ARCHIVE = LOWER-COST RETENTION

sections.title: GSA Scenario Recognition
bullets: Unknown short-term workload with no commitment → On-Demand
Predictable long-running EC2 workload → Reserved Instances
Commit to consistent compute usage and want flexible savings → Savings Plans
Physical-server control for licensing → Dedicated Host
Single-customer hardware without host-level control → Dedicated Instances
Guarantee EC2 capacity in a particular Availability Zone → Capacity Reservation
Large data transfers between Regions → Consider data-transfer charges
Rarely accessed data needs long-term retention → Consider lower-cost archival storage tiers or classes
sections.callout: Find the defining workload requirement first.

sections.title: Maestro Recognition Sheet
bullets: Data entering AWS → Often no transfer charge
Data leaving AWS or crossing Regions → May incur charges
Storage price → Match tier to access pattern
sections.callout: NOW · COMMIT · INTERRUPT · SAVE · HOST · ISOLATE · RESERVE · IN · OUT · ARCHIVE
